exposure: Intraperitoneal closed-suction drain use during cesarean delivery
outcome: Interval to relaparotomy due to intraperitoneal bleeding
cohort: 16,581 women undergoing cesarean delivery (excluding cesarean hysterectomy and hollow viscus injury)
finding: While drain use during cesarean delivery was associated with a shorter time to relaparotomy for intraperitoneal hemorrhage, it also led to a higher risk of puerperal fever and a 0.5% risk of relaparotomy for drain removal.
